title: Air India to Restore Most Suspended International Routes From September as Summer Cuts End
excerpt: Tata-backed carrier says flights from September are already on sale, but Chicago and Washington routes remain grounded due to aircraft constraints and Pakistan airspace closure.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India will restore most suspended international routes starting September.
  • Chicago and Washington routes remain suspended due to aircraft constraints.
  • Pakistan airspace closure is a major operational challenge for Air India.
  • Air India has been operating reduced schedules since June due to high jet fuel prices.

  • Air India expects to restore most suspended domestic and international capacity from September, with flights already on sale in booking systems.
  • Services to Chicago and Washington will remain suspended due to aircraft availability constraints.
  • The closure of Pakistan's airspace remains the airline's biggest operational challenge, though reopening of Iranian and Iraqi airspace would provide relief.
  • The carrier has been operating reduced schedules since June due to record-high jet fuel prices and airspace restrictions caused by the US-Iran conflict.

Air India will restore the bulk of its temporarily suspended international routes from September, bringing relief to passengers who have faced reduced frequencies and outright cancellations on key corridors since June, according to the airline's Chief Commercial and Transformation Officer Nipun Aggarwal.

Speaking on the sidelines of a tourism conference organised by the Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism & Hospitality on Friday, Aggarwal said the network rationalisation was always planned as a three-month measure covering June, July, and August only.

What's Coming Back

"We have cut the capacity only for June, July and August. From September onwards, most of the flights are already on sale," Aggarwal said. The statement provides the clearest timeline yet for when passengers can expect normal service to resume on routes that have been thinned or suspended since the airline announced its broadest schedule pullback under Tata Group ownership.

The cuts have been extensive. Air India halved Delhi-Paris services from 14 to seven weekly flights. Delhi-Singapore dropped from 24 to 14 weekly flights. Routes to Copenhagen, Vienna, Zurich, and Rome all saw reduced frequencies. Flights to Melbourne and Sydney fell from daily to four or five times per week. North American corridors — including Delhi-San Francisco and Delhi-Toronto — were significantly curtailed.

Chicago and Washington Stay Grounded

Two notable exceptions will not return in September. Services to Chicago and Washington are expected to remain suspended because of aircraft availability constraints. These are key corridors for the Indian-American community, particularly the large populations in the Chicago metropolitan area and the Washington, D.C. region. Passengers on these routes will need to continue connecting through other Air India hubs or using competing carriers.

The airline attributed the suspensions to a combination of factors: record-high jet fuel prices for international operations, which have been exacerbated by the US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions, and ongoing airspace restrictions that force longer routings and inflate operating costs.

"The continuing closure of Pakistan's airspace remains the biggest operational challenge for the airline."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

The Pakistan Airspace Problem

Pakistan closed its airspace to Indian carriers as bilateral tensions escalated, forcing Air India to reroute flights between India and destinations to the west — including Europe, the Middle East, and North America — through longer southern corridors. The detours add hours to flight times and significantly increase fuel burn and crew costs.

Aggarwal noted that while the reopening of Iranian and Iraqi airspace would provide significant relief, there is little the airline can do beyond adapting schedules until the geopolitical situation improves. With the US-Iran conflict intensifying this week — Iran has resumed its Strait of Hormuz blockade and attacked Gulf state airports — the airspace picture remains volatile.

Scale of Operations

Even with the cuts, Air India has maintained more than 1,200 international flights per month, operating across five continents and serving over 60 international destinations. The airline operates more than 300 aircraft under the Air India Group umbrella, including Air India Express.

The carrier is in the midst of a fleet modernisation programme under Tata Group, with orders placed for new Airbus A350s and Boeing 787s. The widebody delivery timeline will be critical in determining when routes like Chicago and Washington can be economically restored.

What NRIs Should Know

For diaspora travellers planning autumn and winter trips to India, the key takeaway is that most major routes should return to normal frequencies from September 1. Passengers booked on currently suspended routes have been offered alternative flights, free date changes, or full refunds. Those flying to or from Chicago and Washington should plan connections through New York JFK, Newark, or San Francisco for the foreseeable future. The volatile Middle East situation means that schedule changes remain possible with short notice — travellers are advised to book flexible tickets where available.

Challenges Facing Air India
›Chicago and Washington routes remain grounded.
›Record-high jet fuel prices impacting operations.
›Pakistan airspace closure complicates flight routes.
›Geopolitical tensions affecting airspace availability.
